uncovered_scopes: Complete invariant and transition inventory of all three normative roadmaps
Compiler, planner, manifest, CLI and editor invariants
Production installer and migration executors, bootstrap and control-format upgrades
Typed row-function semantics, persisted-proof ABI boundaries and Same
Versioned queue payload transformations, quarantine replay and external effects
Staged uniqueness, offline changes, catch-up and pruning

entries.statement: A migration's processing ABI cannot change after any batch, provisional work or committed target-generation application write; reprocessing uses a later version and fresh generation.
Independently compiled old and new applications read the same logical rows across additive schema versions.
An additive old-version write preserves columns owned by newer versions.
Competing application writes observe transaction boundaries and never publish a partial update.
Only the exact current live queue attempt may renew or publish an outcome; expired and dead claims are not silently revived.
Only the backend holding the non-expiring session boot lock performs install work; an expired observability lease cannot release that lock.

An extra column default is benign only when its supported scalar type and recognized constant cannot execute code or reject an omitted-column insert; arbitrary casts, domains and computations are drift.

Catalog evidence includes behavior-affecting relation, column, constraint, index, trigger and policy properties; isolated property changes are distinguishable without catalog-row OIDs or raw DDL text.
Catalog expressions use one server deparser under an empty search path, with matching types and collations; comparison objects and settings do not survive the probe transaction.
Nonunique indexes are not automatically harmless: expressions, predicates and plain-key width limits can reject old-valid writes; extra indexes require classification and an old-key domain proof.
Retirement waits for retiring claimants only; surviving claimants retain their attempt, status and lease when restamped.
Explicit model time is monotone and bounded arithmetic cannot wrap a lease into validity.
Physical contract follows retirement and the compatibility switch, and an interrupted contract remains resumable.
An index statement and its final catalog verification hold the same backend's shared job lock and admitted version fence.

Contract drains shared job locks and records terminal with its immutable removal version before destructive DDL; DROP waits for that version's compatibility switch, and a stale worker cannot resurrect the job.
Queue claims remain inside the admitted decoder window and never claim a future payload version.
Retirement's coordinator lock excludes a competing expansion.
Every excluded writer is drained before retirement and cannot resume writing after its version is retired.
Retirement commits only after every affected row is accepted at its target generation; accepted batches survive coordinator abort.
Admission and compatibility floors are ordered, monotone and consistent with committed lifecycle evidence.
Row generations advance one step at a time within the permanent smallint generation bound.
Interleavings identify actor and occurrence, reject ambiguous control input, and fail with bounded waits and useful state dumps.
Version identities and classifications are immutable, consecutive and complete; an equal retry remains transaction-safe.
The model distinguishes absent, active-invalid, abandoned-invalid and valid index catalog states.
An index job retains its declared semantic identity; a same-named different catalog object is not adopted.
Index readiness requires the exact expected valid catalog object, not a worker's recorded intention.
Recovery drops only an inactive invalid remnant and preserves an active or successfully completed build.
Initial expansion publishes its lifecycle and admission singleton atomically; a database born at V9 never invents V8 history.
Initial install and additive expansion verify the selected catalog before recording expansion and preserve completed objects across recovery.
The first lock holder persists an immutable initial target; a newer successor completes that target before expanding further.
Scheduling lease tokens increase on takeover and stale executors cannot publish another holder's work.
Only validated lifecycle edges append history and committed history agrees with the admission singleton.
A PostgreSQL matrix lane checks the connected server's actual major before constructing fixtures.
Application and worker roles cannot bypass lifecycle guards by writing control tables or shadowing control functions.
Quarantine records a current rejection after coordinator abort; changed, accepted or deleted rows cannot retain stale evidence.
At floor commit no non-quarantined durable job remains below the new floor.
A strict read buffers its query result and delivers only after successful admission and transaction commit, retaining table locks until then.
Concurrent schema families allocate distinct bounded fence namespaces and UUIDs; aborted or exhausted allocations never replace a committed identity or use a reserved key.
The global fence registry and its identity sequence have the trusted NOLOGIN control owner and no non-owner mutation grants.

A pre-existing registry matches the independent permanent-table, constraint, index and sequence catalog; lookalikes, inheritance, rewrite rules and altered definitions are refused without aborting caller work.
Serving repair chains may be compatible prefixes, but the final-pass executor carries every recorded amendment.
Repair chains are positive, bounded, gap-free and append-only without changing the migration's own identity.
Recorded repairs run in sequence on a rejected row and stop at the first acceptance.
Repairs cannot reinterpret rows already accepted by the frozen transform or apply a stale row evaluation.
The oracle distinguishes row revisions and refuses stale evaluations and revision overflow.
Every normative-roadmap SQL fence explicitly declares whether it is executable, illustrative or a generated snapshot.
The documented bootstrap transaction and contract recipe are generated from the exact fixtures executed by the PostgreSQL tests.
A lagged replica's local floor and catalog cannot authorize a strict application read across primary retirement.
Every registered harness invariant and transition has a named test, every test names an invariant, and every model operation is inventoried.
A failed ready-but-invalid unique index may already reject old-version writes; readiness and cleanup must use actual PostgreSQL catalog states.
Schema versions are positive signed integers and cannot allocate the reserved boot-fence key.
A transforming expansion closes an additive epoch and respects the bounded compatibility window.
